title: Craft N Code Atlas
subtitle: Everything we know, everything we built, every file, zero summaries. Each entry renders its full source and has an OPEN FILE button.

entries.blurb: The map of the whole repo: what lives where, why, and the reading order. Start here.
The new-window reset doc: mission, done list, next steps, operating rules, key facts, file tree, resume command.
The full timeline: every session, every commit, every decision from Aug 13 to now, with hashes and whys.
The all-in window's session record: decisions, builds, audit findings, commits, window-end state.
Every possible topic: 30 domains, 7 shapes, statement grammar, fingerprint protocol.
The 12-wave integration: verified numbers per wave, where each plugs in, stage use.
The 21:30 quick-mount table: 5 mount cards, 25 domain rows, 6 judge attack answers, 3-min script.
Benchmark + eval registry, one per domain, hundreds of named evals, wave-4 verified upgrades.
Stress registry: 7 classes x 30 domains, wave-5 verified standards (p99 SLO, OWASP LLM, Jepsen).
Kavach-grade diligence per domain + wave-verified ammo: fraud 8 numbers, DPDPA, sponsor DNA, funding rails.
5 mountable kits + company flavor matrix + competitor lines per kit (wave-8).
Where AI-built software fails: REPLIT, PocketOS, Pale Fire, MCP poisoning, stage lines, guardrail map.
Frontier benchmark landscape: HCAST, SWE-bench spread, MAST, WebArena + wave-2/4/6 numbers.
The night schedule 20:00 to 09:00: roles, format facts, the three gates (23:00/03:00/05:00), pre-warm rule, 429 watch, kill criteria. Print this.
v2: one-sentence stories per kit, evaluator closing line, fraud numbers block, honesty line. Paste-ready for both gates.
The live numbers ledger: every stat we quote on stage, with sources and wave tags.
The judge attack sheets: hardest questions per kit, verbatim-ready answers, recovery lines.
6 backend drills: skin mount, live data beat, honesty moment, dependency failure, speed runs.
The Rudra ask draft: 2025 Rajasthan state problems + judging format. Cutoff 21:00.
The full playbook: fingerprint, decision tree, kit mount, demo flow, venue rule, 429 watch.
Drill 1: mock problem drops parsed with the machine, all pin to existing kits.
Every channel where announcements land: Unstop, club site, WhatsApp, Telegram, and who watches what.
The Aug 15 session record: waves 15-18, mock drops, build specs 3-4, submission kit v2, window close.
Spec 3: honest badge H1-H6 + feeds F1-F8. Built and verified.
Spec 4: stress bench + deck MCP slide M1-M6. Built and verified.
The UI/UX brief: mode badge, evidence panel, approval queue UX, freshness badge.
The aggressive audit findings: what was wrong, what got fixed, what stayed.
4x 3-minute storyboards with second-level timing and failure beats.
Archived option: hardware demo. NOT a track assumption. Kept for reference.
First recon: what the event is, verified timeline, organizers, open questions.
The live Unstop listing: 402+ teams, Rs 50,000 prize, qualifier has its own problems, contacts verified.
Live API refresh: submission = PPT only (pdf/pptx, 50MB), multiple submissions allowed, judge buttons shortlist/reject/hold/noshow, D3 site live.
The event site internals: admin console is read-only and pitch-first, submission is a plain INSERT, latest entry wins, night canteen is a UI mock.
Original site forensics: the 5 tracks verbatim, overnight timeline, sponsors, Supabase backend.
CSC's dress rehearsal: NEXORA'26 site internals, 6 tracks, the judging stack (Jury Score, redacted review, leaderboard), submission requirements.
The 5 tracks with exact bodies, evidence-based likelihood per track, sponsor-to-track mapping, honest probability table.
Event site forensics: two gates (Unstop 06:00, club site 09:00), admin read-only, submission internals.
OCR of the event brochure: cards, prize pool, venue, rules as printed.
All 9 problems from D3 Fest 2022 verbatim, and the problem-family lineage into 2025 and 2026.
D3 Fest 2023 brochure: 12 events, the 13h overnight hackathon that is the 24h format's ancestor.
D3 Fest 2026 national brochure content.
The 2024 RVCE state round: food safety theme, 3 tracks, 4x25% judging, top-2 advance, 5 participant solutions mapped.
All 20 national finalists of 2025 with projects, repos, challenges, and stacks.
The 2025 state-round map: 11 rounds found, 1,592 total registrations, uniform fee and prize.
2026 state qualifier scan: Rajasthan is the biggest confirmed round, UP is fresh.
The p-society org census: no 2026 solutions repo exists publicly, dead ends closed honestly.
AFTERPACKETS (2025 national winner), TrueMix (2024), GENESIS (Hackfest 2024): full forensics and the winning formula.
AFTERPACKETS code-level: the C++ DPI core, 13 UI screens, the commit timeline by hour, and why it beat EduSynth and PromptBuddy.
Every public participant repo found across all editions, with stacks and dates.
The 6 judges of the 2024 panel, each one's lens, the comparative matrix, and how a project wins THIS panel.
The full CSC MUJ roster: exec committee, coordinators, advisors, and the key organizer profiles.
Tech Society IIIT-B dossiers: the national organizers.
Rabbitt AI: the founder, the products (ChanceRAG, DRIP), the NEXORA partnership, and the talent-funnel playbook.
The 2025 finalists as a threat matrix, the winner's workflow (scope down, rebrand, clean), and the empty-lane strategy.
Org lineage, edition history, people, sponsors, participant numbers across all editions.
How teams lose: 404 repos, empty repos, no deployment, weak pitches, crowded lanes, tooling wars.
2024 rules verbatim plus every sponsor's DNA pulled from their own hackathons (Solution Challenge, LlamaCon, Accenture Innovation, Creative Jam).
The 8-point winning formula, what each sponsor makes and looks for, the hottest tech for a 24h build.
Deep research (78K chars): evidence-mined most likely problem statements, 5 ranked shapes, kill criteria.
Deep research (68K chars): 2025-2026 product launches and verbatim problem shapes per sponsor.
Deep research (62K chars): winner case studies and demo techniques.

Company lanes pass 1 (SURFACE): first-pass sponsor problem shapes.
Our 5 pre-built ideas (BriefLens, Kavach Circle, SignalStory, Kavach, plus one more), sponsor DNA match, and the decision tree for the drop.
What the deep-research runs conclude: the 5 ranked predicted problems, the common denominator pipeline, the 5 portable patterns.
What we still do not know, tiered by value, and how to get it.
The re-audit: 4 corrections to earlier claims, 3 new data points, the verified-clean list.
The intel execution log: how the research was run and scored.
One-page scaffold guide: the pipeline, quickstart, on-the-night flow.
Every scaffold file explained function by function, with production lessons and audit how-to.
Spec of the approval gate + trace viewer: endpoints, tables, acceptance tests. Both built and verified.
Spec of the provider adapter, multimodal adapter, provenance and consent: tests and acceptance. Built and verified.
The pipeline brain: ingest, dedupe, summarize, rank, deadlines, trace ring buffer. 474 lines, fully explained in CODE-WALKTHROUGH.
The approval gate: typed tool registry, policy gate, proposals + audit tables, consent, provenance.
The provider adapter: swap LLM backends via SIGNAL_PROVIDER without touching engine.py.
The multimodal input adapter: text, PDF, image extraction with graceful fallback.
The zero-dependency HTTP server: 14 API endpoints, --fixture and --offline flags.
The dark UI: digest, ranked feed, search, request board, Actions tab, mode badge, trace drawer.
The one-command demo runner: generate the feed, serve the app.
The deck generator: one skeleton, 4 sponsor-shaped decks.

Acceptance suite T1-T6 plus offline regression for trace + fixtures. 12/12 passing.
Acceptance suite P1-P4 for the provider adapter. 9/9 passing.
Acceptance suite M1-M4 for multimodal ingest. 4/4 passing.
Acceptance suite Q1-Q4 for provenance + consent. 4/4 passing.

The live feeds module: HN Firebase + Unstop reg count, freshness badge, --offline mode.
Acceptance suite F1-F4 for feeds + serve --feeds freshness. Verified.

Stress bench: 23/23 checks under load, SLOs, kill-key behavior.
The war-room home: status table, shared scaffold, deep-research wave, remaining work.
The file-by-file index of the whole repo.
